Cross-browser UI test automation

A maintainable Playwright and TypeScript framework using the Page Object Model.

  • 115 tests on Chromium, Firefox, WebKit and a phone profile
  • 94% of 87 manual test cases automated and traced
  • Keyboard and accessibility checks; known site bugs kept as expected-failure tests
  • 0 flaky tests in 345 runs, run on every code change

For you: your key user journeys are re-checked on every release in minutes, in every major browser, instead of by hand.

API test suite from an OpenAPI spec

A Postman and Newman suite for a booking API, proven by mutation testing.

  • 74 requests and 186 assertions: status codes, response structure, login and permissions, bad inputs, security
  • 13 API defects documented
  • 20 deliberately injected faults, all caught by the suite
  • Test data cleans up after itself; secrets removed from reports

For you: a change that breaks your API is caught before your app's users see it, and the suite is proven to notice real mistakes.

An order and checkout backend (GraphQL, PostgreSQL, Redis) with payment and shipping webhooks. The tests send real requests to it and then check the database, not only the answer.

Testing an order backend: webhooks, database and cache

API tests, load tests and mutation testing for a GraphQL order service, run against real PostgreSQL and Redis in CI.

  • 124 tests: the full order state machine, signed webhooks (bad signature, replay, duplicates, out-of-order events), cancellations, returns, 30 customers fighting over 7 items
  • 20 deliberately injected faults, all caught by the suite
  • Load test: healthy to about 2,000 requests per second; the first limit is the Node.js process, not the database; 9 data checks pass on 586 orders afterwards

For you: orders and payments are checked in the database where mistakes are costly (stock, totals, duplicate events), and you learn what breaks first under load.

The tests run on a real Android emulator in GitHub Actions and are repeated to measure how often they fail for no reason. A flow that is wrong on purpose must fail on every run, which proves the checks are real.

Mobile app tests with Maestro

End-to-end tests for a React Native shopping app, from the catalog to a placed order.

  • 10 flows, all passing in about 5.5 minutes, including a full purchase
  • Smoke and regression suites chosen by tag; reusable steps shared between tests
  • Smoke flows repeated 10 times: 40 of 40 passed, no flaky test
  • Android so far; not yet run on iOS or real devices

For you: a release check for your mobile app that runs on every change, with a measured flakiness rate instead of a hope that the tests are stable.

About me

I'm a QA engineer based in Dhaka. I focus on automated tests for web apps and APIs, and on bug reports that developers can act on without having to ask me questions.

Every project on this page is built in the open: it runs automatically on every change and publishes its results, so you can check each number yourself instead of taking my word for it.

How I work

  1. You describe the app

    What it does, how often you release, and what worries you most.

  2. I propose a clear scope

    What will be tested, what you will receive, and a delivery date.

  3. You get evidence, not opinions

    Regular updates, every defect with steps and a screenshot, and everything in a repository you own.
